correctness.rationale: The proof reduces subsequence membership in q ordered permutation blocks to exactly one plus the number of weak descents; necessity is strict monotonicity within a block and sufficiency is explicit earliest-block embedding. In a palindrome, each mirrored adjacent unequal-letter pair contributes exactly one weak descent, equal-letter pairs contribute two, and an even center contributes one. Hence minimum blocks equal 1+half-length parameter+adjacent equalities; binomially counting halfwords proves each length coefficient and the rational generating function. Longest length and factor contrast follow; the dominant generating-function pole yields the exponential growth. tools/verify.py independently compares complete distinct-subsequence histograms in 21 cases and 150 relabelings, and bounded candidate-wise greedy tests. Finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The theorem gives a complete uniform length spectrum for the repeated q-letter permutation, with q>=3 and arbitrary copy count. The closest source (Mahalingam and Pandoh, 2021, Sections 4-5) treats general bounds, an order-two word example for length-three palindromes, and a high-alphabet extremal problem; none entails the full repeated-permutation spectrum. Müllner and Ryzhikov (2019, Sections 2-4) handle lengths of the longest palindromic subsequences and constructions, not exact distinct-subsequence enumerators. Multiple searches of published mathematical records and targeted literature queries returned no same-object formula. Binary alternating length spectra are known separately and are not claimed as new. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: Equivalent closed formulas could exist in unindexed, differently titled, or inaccessible combinatorics-on-words literature; a negative search is not a uniqueness proof.
A general dynamic-programming computation of scattered-palindrome counts exists, but no inspected source derives the uniform symbolic repeated-permutation spectrum.
The binary alternating case is already covered by a separate specialized result and is excluded from the claimed new scope.

value.rationale: This provides a complete symbolic length spectrum, not a one-off evaluation or algorithmic recount, for the canonical infinite family formed by repeated complete alphabet permutations. It identifies a structural minimum-block invariant, a second-order generalized Fibonacci law and exponential scattered-palindrome growth while contiguous palindrome complexity remains exactly q. This sharp disparity motivates the exact object/invariant; the count does not follow from known global high-alphabet maxima or longest-subsequence results. No optimization over all words or broader application is claimed.
